title: Impact of US-China Phase 1 Trade Deal on Singapore’s Economy, Exports and Businesses
what_it_is: Impact of US-China Phase 1 Trade Deal on Singapore’s Economy, Exports and Businesses

sections.label: Local exports decline impact questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how many businesses and employees were affected, whether outreach was made, and progress on expanding export markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of local exports declining in the past nine months (a) how many businesses and employees have been affected in the past year; (b) whether outreach has been made to businesses to assess the impact and assistance they may require to stay afloat; and (c) what progress has been made on efforts to expand our export market in the past year.

sections.label: IMF downgrades 2019 global growth
sections.summary: The IMF downgraded its 2019 global growth forecast five times since October 2018 to 3%, down from 3.6% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) downgraded the 2019 global growth forecast five successive times in each of its quarterly reports since October 2018 to 3%, down from the 3.6% achieved in 2018.

sections.label: Singapore 2019 growth and 2020 forecast
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew 0.7% in 2019, and MTI expects GDP growth of 0.5% to 2.5% ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Advance estimates show that Singapore’s economy grew by 0.7% in 2019, slower than the 3.1% recorded in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Looking ahead, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) expects Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) growth to pick up modestly to between 0.5% and 2.5% on the back of a slight uptick in global economic growth and a gradual recovery in the global electronics cycle.

sections.label: EDB investment commitments in 2019
sections.summary: EDB attracted more than $8 billion of investment commitments in 2019 despite global economic uncertainties, citing Singapore's strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our stable political environment and united leadership empower us with the capacity to plan for the long term; the rule of law and pro-innovation regulatory environment provide certainty for businesses to thrive; our superior connectivity with the rest of the world allows us to look to the world for opportunities; our strong tripartite partnership and a skilled workforce that continually upgrades and generates new ideas, and acquires new skillsets and knowledge that can redefine what is possible for a country with no natural hinterland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why the Economic Development Board (EDB) has attracted more than $8 billion of investment commitments in 2019, despite the global economic uncertainties.

sections.label: MRA grants to 800 companies
sections.summary: As of September 2019, 800 companies received grant support for overseas market forays through the MRA scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Last year, as of September 2019, we gave out 800 companies grant support for their forays into overseas markets through the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) scheme.

sections.label: Worker outcomes condition for EDG funding
sections.summary: From 1 April 2020, commitment to worker outcomes becomes a mandatory condition for companies applying for EDG funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To further strengthen the linkage between enterprise transformation and benefits to our workers, we will include commitment to worker outcomes as a mandatory condition for companies that apply for EDG funding from 1 April 2020.

sections.label: RCEP negotiations and India
sections.summary: The 15 RCEP countries concluded tax-based negotiations and committed to sign in Vietnam in 2020, with the door open for India to join.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second question, on RCEP, last year, at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit, the 15 RCEP countries have essentially concluded all the tax-based negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The leaders of the 15 countries have given their commitment to sign the agreement in Vietnam in 2020 and all the officials are working hard to realise that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The door remains open for India to join RCEP and I think that is the common position for all the 15 member states.
